memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'The priest is to wave the two lambs before the LORD as a wave
offering, together with the bread of the firstfruits. They are a sacred
offering to the LORD for the priest. On that same day you are to
proclaim a sacred assembly and do no regular work. This is to be a
lasting ordinance for the generations to come, wherever you live'"
- Lev 23:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The priests received a portion from what the people brought. They owned
no farmland of their own; their livelihood came through the offerings
of God's people. This was God's arrangement, not an accident.

Dear friend, the New Testament carries this principle forward. Paul
writes that those who preach the gospel should receive their living
from the gospel (1 Cor 9:14), and he tells the Galatians that the one
who receives instruction in the word should share all good things with
their instructor (Gal 6:6).

There is something healthy about a community that supports those who
serve it spiritually. It creates mutual dependence. The people are fed
spiritually; the servants are supported practically. Neither can
pretend they do not need the other.

Let this prompt a practical thought. Is there a pastor, a Sunday school
teacher, a worship leader, a missionary in your circle whom you could
encourage or support this month? Many serve quietly with very little
recognition.

And notice again: "wherever you live." This was not only for those near
the temple. Wherever God's people were scattered, this rhythm of
worship and mutual care travelled with them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who has served me spiritually that I have never thanked?
2. Am I supporting gospel work with my resources as well as my words?
3. How can I encourage someone in ministry this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for those who have taught and cared for me
spiritually. Show me how to support and encourage them well. Amen.
